verdict.summary: Composio has no managed Shopify app, so you have to register your own. A custom-distribution app works on one store (or one Plus organization, or development stores) with no Shopify approval. Any public app, including an unlisted one, needs App Store review before production merchants can install it. Shopify also reviews protected customer data and some scopes separately, and from January 1, 2027 public apps must use expiring offline tokens.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min for a custom/dev-store app; 1-3 days to prepare a public App Store submission (listing, privacy policy, screencast, compliance)
verdict.approval_wait: none for custom distribution; public review has no published turnaround, reported at 1 week to 3-4 weeks

gates.name: Development store install
gates.unlocks: You can connect your own development store through your own app via Composio.
limits: Must be tested on a development store; Shopify tells developers to create a new app and test it on a development store
The distribution method (custom vs public) can't be changed after you select it

gates.name: Custom distribution (single store / Plus organization / development stores)
gates.unlocks: Real installs on one merchant store, or on stores in one Plus organization, with no Shopify approval. A public app before review can still be installed on development stores under the same partner account.
limits: Custom distribution is limited to a single store, stores in one Plus organization, or development stores
Custom apps can't charge merchants through Shopify's app billing system
An unlisted public app is still reviewed; unlisted only hides the listing
Community report: an unreviewed public app with billing showed an 'under review' block even when installed from the Dev Dashboard, while dev-store installs under the same partner account still worked
Protected customer data (e.g. customer name/email/phone/address) is reviewed separately from scopes

gates.name: Public distribution (Shopify App Store review)
gates.unlocks: Any merchant can install the app on production stores (listed or unlisted).
limits: Requires registering for the Shopify App Store (one-time fee)
Status flow: Draft -> Submitted -> Reviewed -> Published; a failed submission moves to Paused and must be resubmitted

From Jan 1, 2027 public apps must use expiring offline access tokens (expire after 60 min). Apps still on non-expiring tokens are delisted and blocked from new installs on that date, and their API calls get HTTP 403 from April 1, 2027
Scopes labelled as requiring approval can't be declared until Shopify approves them
gates.time_to_reach: No official turnaround; plan for at least a week, with reports of 3-4 weeks

steps.title: Sign in to the Shopify Dev Dashboard / Partner account
steps.detail: Sign in at dev.shopify.com/dashboard with your Shopify Partner identity. Since January 1, 2026, new custom apps can't be created in the Shopify admin, so all new apps are built in the Dev Dashboard.
gotchas: The Partner account prerequisites (cost, business verification) are not confirmed from a Shopify-owned page.

steps.title: Create a development store for testing
steps.detail: Create a development store under your partner account. Shopify recommends testing new apps on development stores, and the App Store listing later asks for a demo development store link.

steps.title: Decide on a distribution method before you set it
steps.detail: Choose Custom distribution for a single store, stores in one Plus organization, or development stores. It needs no Shopify approval. Choose Public if arbitrary merchants must install the app. Public requires App Store registration (one-time fee) and review, even if the app is unlisted.
gotchas: You can't change the distribution method after you select it.
Custom apps can't use Shopify's app billing system.

steps.title: Create the app and register the redirect URL
steps.detail: In the Dev Dashboard, create a new app and enter its name, app URL and redirection URLs. Paste the exact callback URL from your Composio Shopify auth config as an allowed redirection URL.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The complete redirect_uri sent in the authorize request must match an allowed redirection URL exactly, or the authorization fails.

steps.title: Trim the scope list to what the agent needs
steps.detail: Start from Composio's default list and remove anything the agent doesn't use. A write scope already grants read access to the same resource, so drop the matching read scope. Note any scope that Shopify labels as needing approval. Merchants see every requested permission on the OAuth grant screen, and Shopify restricts scopes for apps with no legitimate use for the data.

values.label: Scopes
values.value: Minimal comma-separated list, e.g. read_products,write_orders (only what you use)

gotchas: Requesting unnecessary scopes is a reported reason for App Store rejection.

steps.title: Add client credentials to Composio
steps.detail: Copy the app's client ID and client secret from the Dev Dashboard into a Composio Shopify auth config, along with your trimmed scopes. Shopify OAuth runs per shop: the authorize URL is built on the store's own domain with client_id, scope, redirect_uri and state, so each connection needs the shop subdomain.

steps.title: Install on the development store and run a test authorization
steps.detail: Install the app on your development store from the Installs section of the app overview page (Install app). Then start a Composio connection for that store's subdomain and confirm the grant screen appears and a token is issued.
gotchas: With an invalid client_id, the bare shopify.com authorize endpoint redirected to admin.shopify.com instead of returning a clear OAuth error, so check the client ID carefully.
There is no OIDC discovery document to auto-configure from.

steps.title: Request approval for labelled scopes and protected customer data
steps.detail: For scopes labelled as requiring approval, contact Shopify Support with a description of your app and why it needs each scope (an agent can draft the justification). Protected customer data access, such as customer name, email, phone and address, goes through a separate review. Without it, the related fields come back null.
gotchas: Declaring a scope does not grant protected customer data access.

steps.title: Confirm expiring offline access tokens work end to end
steps.detail: Public apps must use expiring offline access tokens for Admin API calls from January 1, 2027. These tokens expire after 60 minutes and rotate. Check that tokens obtained through Composio refresh correctly over a period longer than an hour.
gotchas: If a public app still uses non-expiring tokens, it is delisted and blocked from new installs on Jan 1, 2027, and its API calls get HTTP 403 from April 1, 2027. Custom apps are excluded from this requirement.

steps.title: Prepare the App Store listing and reviewer materials
steps.detail: Draft the privacy policy (required), an app name of 30 characters or fewer that leads with your brand (not 'Shopify'), 3-6 desktop screenshots at 1600x900, a 1200x1200 icon, and a demo development store link. Also prepare test credentials and a screencast for reviewers, and make sure the GDPR/compliance webhooks respond.
gotchas: Missing test credentials or screencast is a listed review failure.
Shopify's official list of mandatory compliance webhooks wasn't fetched; check it before you submit.

steps.title: Check install, OAuth and quality requirements before you submit
steps.detail: On install, the app must redirect merchants to the OAuth grant screen immediately, not in a pop-up, and must authorize before any other step. It must have no fatal errors or broken UI after install, and must not lower Lighthouse performance scores by more than 10 points.

steps.title: Register for the App Store and submit for review
steps.detail: Pay the one-time Shopify App Store registration fee and submit the app. Its status then moves from Draft to Submitted.

steps.title: Wait for review and fix any requested changes
steps.detail: Shopify publishes no turnaround time. Third-party guides say to plan for at least a week, and one developer reported 3-4 weeks. If the app fails core requirements it moves to Paused, and you get an email listing the changes to make before you resubmit.

requirements.item: Allowed redirection URL matching the Composio callback exactly
requirements.detail: The full redirect_uri used in the authorize request must be registered in the Dev Dashboard.

requirements.item: App created in the Dev Dashboard (not the Shopify admin)
requirements.detail: New custom apps can't be created in the Shopify admin from January 1, 2026.
Custom distribution allows one store, one Plus organization, or development stores with no approval. Public distribution requires App Store review.

requirements.item: Scope approval / protected customer data approval
requirements.detail: Scopes labelled as requiring approval need Shopify Support sign-off. Protected customer data fields are reviewed separately and come back null without approval.

requirements.item: Privacy policy, listing assets, demo store
requirements.detail: Privacy policy is required. Shopify recommends 3-6 screenshots at 1600x900, a 1200x1200 icon, an app name of 30 characters or fewer, and a demo development store link.
Mandatory for public apps from January 1, 2027. Tokens expire after 60 minutes and rotate.

requirements.item: Working install/OAuth flow, test credentials and screencast
requirements.detail: The app must redirect to the grant screen, not use a pop-up for OAuth, and not error after install. Reviewers need test credentials and a screencast.

scopes.effect: Each write scope already grants read access to the same resource, so drop the duplicate read_* scope.
Access to protected customer data is reviewed separately from scope declaration. Public apps need review for this data.
Since Dec 10, 2025, web pixel payloads return null for these fields unless the app is approved for the scope.
You can't declare these until Shopify approves them. Contact Shopify Support with a justification.

blockers.symptom: Merchant install blocked with 'This app is under review', even from the Dev Dashboard
blockers.cause: A public app that hasn't passed review can't be installed on production stores. Dev-store installs under the same partner account still work.
blockers.fix: Test on development stores, switch to a custom-distribution app for a single store, or complete App Store review.

blockers.symptom: An unlisted app still requires review
blockers.cause: Unlisted (limited visibility) apps are still public apps with the same requirements.
blockers.fix: Use custom distribution if you only need one store or one Plus organization; otherwise submit for review.

blockers.symptom: App status changes to Paused after submission
blockers.cause: The app failed core requirements, for example the install doesn't redirect to the grant screen, errors after install, missing test credentials or screencast, or billing outside Shopify's billing system.
blockers.fix: Apply the changes listed in Shopify's email and resubmit.

blockers.symptom: App delisted and new installs blocked from Jan 1, 2027; API calls return 403 from April 1, 2027
blockers.cause: The public app still uses non-expiring offline access tokens.
blockers.fix: Migrate to expiring offline tokens and verify that refresh works through Composio.

blockers.symptom: Customer name/email/phone/address fields come back null
blockers.cause: The app isn't approved for protected customer data scopes.
blockers.fix: Request protected customer data access and approval for the relevant scopes.

blockers.symptom: Rejection for app name, scopes or compliance webhooks
blockers.cause: Reported causes: an app name containing 'Shopify', unnecessary scopes, or missing or broken GDPR webhook endpoints.
blockers.fix: Rename the app to lead with your own brand (30 characters or fewer), trim scopes, and implement the compliance webhooks.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Shopify, so you must register your own app in the Dev Dashboard and give Composio its client ID and secret. Add Composio's callback URL (shown in your auth config) as an allowed redirection URL. Composio's default scope list is broad. Trim it, because write scopes already include read access and customer/order data triggers a separate protected-data review. OAuth runs per shop ({shop}.myshopify.com), so each connection needs the store subdomain. For your own store or one Plus organization, custom distribution avoids review entirely. Choose public distribution only if arbitrary merchants must connect.
